newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs welcome Commission's fraud control scheme.
newsitem.headline: MEPs welcome Commission's fraud control scheme.

text.p: The European Parliament welcomed on Friday a plan to improve the management of European Union money, in an attempt to combat fraud.
But Euro-MPs asked for improvements in the scheme.

They demanded the European Commission impose penalities on those caught for financial irregularities and said it should gather more detailed financial information on the way EU money is spent on agriculture, regional and social projects.

The European Commission launched the Sound and Efficient Financial Management scheme (SEM 2000) in January 1995 to tackle weaknesses in the way the Commission and the national authorities manage the EU budget.
The effort is being spearheaded by Budget Commissioner Erkki Liikanen and Anti-Fraud Commissioner Anita Gradin.
Rapporteur Joan Colom i Naval said SEM 2000 signalled "a major change in the Commission's approach to management problems".
The Commission had abandoned the smugness with which it hitherto greeted complaints about fraud from the parliament and the European Court of Auditors, the Spanish Socialist said in his report.
